sections.html:
Halifax County runs along the North Carolina line in southern Virginia. The town of Halifax is the seat, South Boston is the biggest town, and Scottsburg and Virgilina are the other two incorporated towns. At 830 square miles it is a large county, so a rural parcel here can be far from any town office.

Population was 34,022 in 2020 and is estimated at 33,447 now, down from a 2000 count of 37,355. There were 17,275 housing units in 2020, 14.9% of them vacant, and 70.8% of occupied homes were owner-occupied. Older owners and many one-person households tend to produce estate sales and empty houses, and a vacant inherited house still gets a tax bill every year.

South Boston has a wrinkle that can touch paperwork. It was an independent city through the 1990 census and rejoined Halifax County as a town in 1995, so an older record that mentions the city of South Boston should go to the Commissioner of the Revenue to confirm which office holds the parcel today.

The Treasurer collects and the Commissioner of the Revenue is the chief tax authority and keeps real estate ownership records. Both offices are at 1030 Mary Bethune Street in Halifax.

2026 taxRateDue
Real estate$0.50 per $100 of valueJune 5 and December 5
Personal property$3.85 per $100December 5
Machinery and tools$1.26 per $100December 5
  • Treasurer, Suite 103: 434-476-3318, open weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Commissioner of the Revenue, Suite 104: 434-476-3314, open weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Halifax real estate bills fall due June 5 and December 5, while personal property and machinery and tools are due December 5. In a year when the rate is voted late, the Treasurer can mail bills later and extend the first date, so watch the Treasurer's page for a posted notice.

The Treasurer posts fees for paying by card: 2.50% on credit and debit cards, with a $2.00 minimum, and a flat $1.50 for eCheck payments. A check or an in-person payment skips the charge.

The Treasurer also publishes a list of real estate being sold for unpaid tax. Ask the office what the current list covers, and call right away if your parcel number appears on it.

The Commissioner runs a Real Estate Tax Relief Program that discounts the bill for elderly or permanently disabled owners who meet income and net worth tests. It reaches the dwelling and a single acre around it.

  • As of December 31 of the prior year you were either 65 or permanently and totally disabled.
  • On that same date the home was yours and your residence.
  • Gross combined income is capped at $22,000, and income of relatives living in the house counts once it passes $8,500.
  • Net worth is capped at $60,000, leaving out the house and one acre.

A county can revise these caps, so verify today's figures with the Commissioner first. The same office has forms for a disabled veteran real estate tax exemption and for a land use program.

The Commissioner's page links a 2026 Real Estate Assessment Appeal Application, so that form is the place to begin.

A separate state rule gives a period to request a correction: three years from the close of the tax year, or one year after the assessment date, whichever ends last. For real estate it applies when the commissioner slipped, or when a general reassessment produced a factual mistake. Before you file, gather the parcel number, the assessed value and comparable sales, and call 434-476-3314 with questions.

Under state law a real estate tax lien jumps the queue, outranking all other liens, and remains on the property until the locality has its money. Whoever buys at a sale, or a foreclosure trustee, must see proceeds applied to taxes, with penalties and interest counted in.

On a standard sale the title company requests the Treasurer's payoff and settles it from your funds. Ask for the number on paper, and check whether the December half has been billed.

  1. Call the Treasurer at 434-476-3318 for the balance.
  2. Ask the Commissioner at 434-476-3314 about any relief or land use status on the parcel.
  3. Send the written payoff to your closing agent.
  4. Check afterward that the tax account shows paid.

An empty house still collects a tax bill on June 5 and December 5, and the bills pile up fast when no one is checking the mail. If you inherited a Halifax property you do not plan to keep, start by learning what is owed. Phone the Treasurer, give the parcel number, and ask for each unpaid installment along with penalty and interest. Then ask the Commissioner of the Revenue whose name is on the record, because a title company will want the owner of record to match the person signing.

Rental houses with tenants add one more step. Tell the Treasurer's office where to send bills if you no longer live nearby, and let your tenants know a sale is coming so showings can be scheduled around their lease.

Gather what a closing agent will ask for: a copy of the deed or will, any court paperwork naming the person with authority to sell, and recent tax bills. A cash buyer can often close without insisting on repairs, which suits a house that has sat empty for a season or two. Back tax still gets paid at settlement.

Since the tax comes in two halves, a mid-year sale means one installment covers time under both owners. Your contract names the cut-off, and the settlement agent turns that into a credit or a charge on your statement. Read that line carefully. If you paid the June installment, the buyer normally reimburses you for the months after closing. If December is still open, you will probably credit the buyer for your months of ownership.

Because cards carry the 2.50% fee, ask the title company to pay the Treasurer by check or wire. Expect the office to confirm payment in writing, and keep that confirmation with your closing papers.

Common Halifax sales include inherited farmhouses, rentals with tenants, vacant homes in smaller towns and houses that need repairs. Whether the Clerk of the Circuit Court, who records deeds, can find a clean chain of title matters most with old family land, so ask for that search early.

Cash Home Buyers CA buys Halifax County houses as-is, with back tax paid from the proceeds at closing. A cash sale skips the repairs and the showings, though the lien rules above apply no matter who buys.

faqs.q: What is the Halifax County real estate tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's page lists $0.50 per $100 of value for real estate in 2026.

faqs.q: When are Halifax County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 and December 5. Personal property and machinery and tools are due December 5.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Halifax County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Commissioner of the Revenue at 434-476-3314. Call the Treasurer at 434-476-3318 for balances and payments.

faqs.q: Does Halifax County offer tax relief for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. The Commissioner runs a program for owners 65 or older or permanently disabled who meet income and net worth limits, covering the house and up to one acre.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Halifax County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so request a payoff from the Treasurer before the closing date.
